query: What are the real-world risks and benefits of using synthetic data to train or fine-tune large language models? Focus on data quality, bias, and evaluation.

sub_questions.text: What types of data quality issues can arise when using synthetic data to train large language models?
How does synthetic data impact the presence of bias in large language models, particularly in terms of representation and perpetuation?
What evaluation metrics can be used to assess the performance of large language models trained on synthetic data in real-world scenarios?
Can synthetic data exacerbate existing biases in large language models, and if so, what are the implications for fairness and transparency?
What are the real-world benefits of using synthetic data to train or fine-tune large language models, particularly in terms of cost savings and data protection?
